name: Badger Plastics & Supply Inc
old_description: We founded our business in 1984 to address the plastic-related needs of industries across Wisconsin. Over the years, we have earned the patronage of countless customers because of our skill in machining and fabrication. Moreover, numerous companies have come to depend on us due to our expertise in field service and installation.
about:
Badger Plastics & Supply was founded in 1984 in Plover, Wisconsin, to serve the plastic-related needs of industries across the state. The company began as a distributor of mechanical and industrial plastics and later added in-house machining and fabrication capabilities.

Today the firm operates a machine shop equipped with a 60" x 120" Haas gantry mill, seven vertical machining centers, three CNC turning centers, manual lathes, manual mills, two CNC panel saws, and plastics welders. It produces custom machined and fabricated parts from customer samples, drawings, or even rough sketches, and supplies sheets, rods, tubes, and industrial liners. A traveling sales force covers Wisconsin, eastern Minnesota, and upper Michigan, while a dedicated lining crew performs installations throughout the United States.

The company serves foundry and paper industry applications, along with broader industrial manufacturing customers. Its liner products are used in trucks and industrial equipment, and its machining services support one-off prototypes through production runs of a thousand pieces or more.

Badger Plastics emphasizes personal service and flexibility, promising to do what it takes to meet customer specifications and schedules. The company highlights quick turnaround times, attention to detail on every order, and a willingness to tackle unusual requests that other suppliers decline.

name: Ball Packaging Products
old_description: Since 2011, The Ball Foundation, the philanthropic extension of Ball Corporation, has amplified Ball’s organizational values through community partnerships. Today, The Ball Foundation supports over 15 community organizations dedicated to recycling education and infrastructure; science, technology, engineering and mathematics in manufacturing; and disaster relief and preparedness.
about:
Ball Packaging Products, operating as part of Ball Corporation, is headquartered in Westminster, Colorado. The company maintains a global manufacturing footprint spanning 65-plus plants across 49 countries, with a workforce of approximately 16,000 employees. While the exact founding date of the corporation is not provided in the source material, the business has grown into a major supplier of aluminum packaging.

The company produces aluminum beverage cans, bottles, aerosol cans, ends, and aerosol containers for a range of consumer occasions. Its manufacturing scale is substantial: more than 108 billion units are shipped annually. The product portfolio includes standard and specialty cans for beer, water, and soda, as well as aluminum bottles designed for sporting events and concert venues. A second-generation ReAl® aerosol container technology targeting 75 percent recycled content is slated for launch by 2030.

Primary customers are in the beverage industry, including brands packaging beer, water, and carbonated soft drinks. The company also serves the aerosol market and partners with venues such as stadiums and concert halls. Beyond commercial sales, Ball collaborates with supply-chain partners to advance recycling infrastructure and has set a 2030 goal of achieving a 90 percent global recycling rate for aluminum beverage cans, bottles, and cups, along with an 85 percent average recycled content in its aluminum feedstock.

The Ball Foundation, established in 2011, extends the company’s community impact through grants focused on recycling education, STEM in manufacturing, and disaster relief. The corporation states that its differentiation lies in global scale, sustainability commitments, and innovations such as digital printing on cans and the ReAl® aerosol technology.

name: Bally Ribbon Mills
old_description: Design, development, and manufacturer of specialized engineered woven webbing, tapes, and specialty fabrics.
about:
Bally Ribbon Mills operates from Bally, Pennsylvania, where it has manufactured narrow woven fabrics since 1923. The company began as a specialist in engineered webbing, tapes, and specialty fabrics, and has remained a U.S.-based producer throughout its history.

The firm designs, develops, and weaves a range of products including narrow tapes, webbing, seamless tubular materials, 2-D and 3-D structural shapes, braided structures, and multi-layer composites. Production relies on shuttle looms, needle looms, Jacquard looms, braiding equipment, and specialty broad looms capable of widths up to 72 inches. Post-weave operations cover dyeing, finishing (heat setting, resin treatments, PTFE, silicone, flame retardant), strap cutting, hole punching, sonic welding, and minor sub-assembly. The company states it runs from prototype to full-scale production, though facility size and headcount are not disclosed.

Customers span aerospace, defense, medical, safety, automotive, commercial, and industrial sectors. In aerospace and defense, BRM supplies Mil-Spec webbing and tapes (Mil-W-4088, Mil-DTL-5038K, Mil-W-5625K, Mil-T-87130) that are Berry Amendment compliant. Medical clients receive Class I–III device components such as orthopedic strapping, prosthetic textiles, and dental biotextiles. Safety-market products meet UL and NFPA standards for structural, proximity, and wildland fire-fighting gear.

name: Baltimore Aircoil Company, Inc.
old_description: BAC creates sustainable comfort cooling, process cooling, and refrigeration solutions for the most essential and demanding environments on earth.
about:
Baltimore Aircoil Company (BAC) is headquartered in Milford, Delaware, and traces its origins to 1938 when a single cooling coil was hand-built in a founder’s garage. The company has since evolved into an employee-owned enterprise, with its workforce of more than 2,000 global team members holding ownership stakes.

BAC designs and manufactures sustainable comfort cooling, process cooling, and refrigeration equipment for demanding environments. Its product portfolio includes evaporative condensers, adiabatic coolers such as the Trillium™ TRFS for large-scale data centers, modular hybrid coolers like the Nexus® line with integrated PuriStream™ water treatment, and a range of replacement parts supported by inspection services. The company operates globally, though specific facility sizes and production volumes are not disclosed.

The company serves a variety of industries, with explicit focus on heavy industrial and energy sectors. Recent project announcements highlight deployments in large-scale data centers, while its refrigeration piping manuals target industrial refrigeration system designers. Customers range from original equipment manufacturers to end-users seeking full-lifecycle support from initial selection through decades of operation.

BAC’s stated mission is to “continually advance truly sustainable cooling – inspired by nature, powered by our people.” The firm emphasizes balancing water and energy savings, a commitment dating to its first coil, and frames its differentiation around a coordinated, non-transactional process aimed at getting the solution right the first time and maintaining performance for decades. Core values include courage, innovation, responsibility, and trust.

name: Bapko Metal Fabricators
old_description: BAPKO Metal Inc. is a self-performing contractor specializing in miscellaneous steel and architectural metal fabrication and installation. Founded in 1978, we have developed strong partnerships with leading General Contractors across California who rely on our experienced team for innovative solutions, client-centric service, and value-added expertise.
about:
BAPKO Metal Inc. is headquartered in Orange, California, and has operated there since its founding in 1978. The company began as a partnership, transitioned to family ownership for 28 years, then to single ownership before becoming 100 % employee‑owned in its 41st year of operation. This ownership structure underpins a family‑centric culture that the firm says drives its growth and financial resilience.

The firm is a self‑performing contractor that fabricates and installs miscellaneous steel and architectural metalwork. Its services span estimating, design‑assist, 3D BIM modeling (using Tekla Structures), laser scanning, project management, and full‑scale production in over 55,000 sq ft of shop and office space across multiple buildings. Two dedicated divisions handle structural steel and high‑end architectural metals such as stainless steel, bronze, aluminum, and glass.

BAPKO works primarily for general contractors throughout California on commercial, healthcare, educational, industrial, hospitality, and sports‑entertainment projects. Notable installations include the Gaylord Pacific Resort & Convention Center in Chula Vista, the Intuit Dome (Clippers Arena) in Inglewood, and the Din Tai Fung restaurant at Downtown Disney in Anaheim.

The company emphasizes its all‑in‑one, self‑perform model as a differentiator, citing proactive project management, rapid turnaround, and the integration of emerging technologies like 3D laser scanning. Employee ownership is presented as a source of financial stability and a commitment to long‑term client relationships.

name: Barber Packaging Company
old_description: Family-owned and operated since 1989, we believe in building true partnerships.
about:
Barber Packaging Company was founded in 1989 in Bangor, Michigan, as a family-owned and operated business. The company began with a focus on building long-term partnerships through engineered packaging solutions.

The company provides a full-service approach to protective packaging, covering design and engineering using CAD technology, rapid prototyping, manufacturing, validation and testing, and program management. Its product range includes returnable packaging made from steel, wood, plastics, textiles, and foam; expendable packaging for export and retail; work-in-process material handling systems; and service/backup packaging. Manufacturing capabilities include CNC abrasive wire, CNC oscillating and tangential cutting, and automated assembly.

Barber serves a variety of industries that require protective packaging, though specific sectors are not listed publicly. Customers include OEMs and assembly plants needing intra-plant material handling, export shipping solutions, and custom protective packaging for product protection.

The company differentiates itself through "The Barber Way," a relationship-based philosophy emphasizing simple coordination, faster turnaround, cost savings, and single-source solutions. Its in-house design team and accredited lab partnerships enable quick iteration and compliance testing, while program management ensures projects stay on schedule and budget.

name: Bardot Plastics
old_description: Three generations of expertise delivering precision parts since 1973. Our modern facility with state-of-the-art equipment ensures quality at every step.
about:
Bardot Plastics operates from a modern facility in Easton, Pennsylvania, where it has been manufacturing precision injection-molded parts since 1973. The company was founded by J. Lee Boucher and remains a third-generation family business, now led by his sons Chris, Jim, and Rick Boucher. What began as a vision for superior injection molding has grown into a full-service operation built on the principle of “making it right the first time.”

The shop specializes in large-tonnage molding, running presses up to 1,760 tons to produce large, complex components that many molders cannot accommodate. Its end-to-end capabilities cover design consultation, integrated tooling (single-cavity, multi-cavity, and family molds), insert molding, sonic welding, sub-assembly, and in-house packaging and fulfillment. A 120-ton central chilling unit and robotic part-removal systems support consistent quality across prototype and high-volume runs, working with both engineered and non-engineered resins.

Bardot serves a diverse industrial base including office furniture, lawn and garden, waste and recycling, industrial equipment, military, construction, agricultural, and commercial markets. Customers rely on the company for ergonomic workplace components, durable industrial parts, military-spec precision pieces, weather-resistant outdoor products, structural components, and agricultural parts built to withstand harsh environments.

The company differentiates itself through continuous technology investment — exemplified by the recent chilling unit installation — and a single-point-of-contact project management model. Its guiding principles of excellence, innovation, sustainability, and partnership reflect a heritage of delivering tight tolerances and dimensional stability regardless of part size or complexity.

old_description: Barrington Wood Works established in April 2018. We have several years of experience in the Custom Millwork Industry.  We work with clients, designers and architects directly, creating shop drawings for any project that is needed with the most professional level of finish.
about:
Barrington Wood Works LLC was founded in April 2018 in Lake Barrington, Illinois. The company entered the custom millwork industry with a focus on direct collaboration with clients, designers, and architects, producing shop drawings for each project.

The shop handles custom millwork design, CNC machining, factory finishing, fabrication, installation, and field touch‑ups, all performed at its Lake Barrington facility. It also offers semi‑custom cabinetry and pre‑installs assemblies to simplify final installation. Processes include hand scraping, machining, and faux finishes.

The firm serves both commercial and residential customers across the Greater Chicagoland area, including communities such as Arlington Heights, Barrington, Lake Forest, Naperville, and Winnetka. It works directly with designers and architects and supplies cabinetry from brands such as Crystal Cabinets, Fabuwood Cabinets, and Showplace Cabinetry.

The company emphasizes high‑quality craftsmanship and materials with a quick turnaround, positioning its in‑house fabrication and finishing as a way to maintain control over the final product’s finish and fit.

name: Basic E Inc.
old_description: is the best choice for fast skilled repair work on a variety of industrial equipment.
about:
Basic E Inc. operates from Charlotte, Vermont, where it maintains a 34,000-square-foot warehouse stocked with 86,000 line items. The company's founding date and ownership details are not publicly disclosed.

The business functions primarily as a franchised distributor of obsolete and military-specification electronic and electrical components for electric generating utilities. It stocks passives, electro-mechanicals, actives, wire-and-cable, and MIL-SPEC parts from franchised lines such as Barker Microfarads and Capteks, all backed by certificates of compliance and full traceability. Beyond distribution, Basic E provides repair services for industrial equipment, custom cable and harness assembly to customer specifications, and an asset-recovery program that purchases surplus new inventory outright.

Its customer base includes more than 35 nuclear power plants and other electric utility operators that rely on hard-to-find replacement parts for critical infrastructure. The company also serves broader industrial markets needing electronic components, motors, valves, relays, circuit boards, and related equipment.

Basic E positions itself as a one-stop source for obsolete parts with rapid turnaround, emphasizing its franchised authorization, traceable documentation, and ability to supply both components and finished cable assemblies from a single facility.

name: Bauer Fabrication & Art Metal
old_description: At Bauer Fabrication & Art Metal based in Waterbury, VT, we take pride in the artistic execution of our customers’ projects. Our fabrication work is custom art, aesthetic as well as utilitarian. Dedicated to the realization of our clients’ unique specifications, we pay extra attention to detail, thereby creating one-of-a-kind pieces.
about:
Bauer Fabrication & Art Metal operates from Waterbury, Vermont, as a metal fabricating and machine shop specializing in architectural metal work, custom furniture, and original artwork. The company serves architects, designers, contractors, and homeowners throughout New England and beyond, with installations in New York City, Boston, Florida, Mississippi, California, and the Virgin Islands.

In its Waterbury facility, the team combines traditional hand-and-eye craftsmanship with a patented thermal-spray-and-wire-mesh process branded as Bauer Art Metal. This proprietary method builds freestanding objects by spraying molten metal, enabling sculptural artwork, memorials, and household items such as sinks and cookware that would otherwise require casting. The shop also provides design services and installation, coordinating with other trades when needed.

Clients include Gossens Bachman Architects, which has commissioned complex stairways and custom sinks, and Planeta Design Group of Boston, a long-term collaborator on boundary-pushing projects. Residential customers such as Howard and Linda Awand have received one-of-a-kind garden fences. The firm works across construction, architectural, residential, and art markets, delivering custom stair rails, staircases, furniture, memorials, and decorative objects.

The company distinguishes itself by welcoming challenging, non-repetitive jobs and by integrating its patented thermal-spray technique with conventional fabrication to create unique textures and forms. Its stated intention is to deliver a finish of excellent and uniform quality on every custom piece.
